title: C01 跨河登高
prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one clean square ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP-DOWN terrain level planning map, entirely overhead, no perspective, no text, no labels, no shadows, no textures, no trees or buildings. Flat solid colors: mountain/rock footprint #777F89, water #39A9DB, walkable open ground #EFEAD8, continuous walking path #E4A33B, destination terrace #BB65CE, start dot #E65050. Important spatial brief C01: an irregular east-west river divides foreground southern bank from northern mountain shoulder. The start is on the southern bank. A broad elevated purple viewing terrace on the northwestern shoulder is the Pull destination. The deep river provides Push by preventing a direct shortcut. There is exactly one crossing on the eastern side. The orange path runs from start along the south bank, across that crossing, then bends back up a broad continuous rock shoulder and ridge to the purple terrace. Behind the terrace place a separate lake basin, with a rock ridge between terrace and lake to provide an adjustable conceal/reveal screen. Mountain footprints form the near/middle/far hierarchy with deliberate open valleys between. Keep path connected and clearly visible on the rock. Paths should be smooth irregular curves, not radial rings. Show full map margins. Shapes should be few, large, irregular but simple enough to convert to polygons. This is a semantic layout proposal with Pull, river barrier, continuous ridge climb and arrival reveal represented by actual spatial relations, not a scenic illustration.

provenance.extraction: HSV masks and contour tracing; topology/height/observer semantics assisted by AI
annotations: 出生、河中心线、跨越、连续路线与POI连接由AI对原图语义标注；灰/紫/湖轮廓来自自动分割。
80m台地和山群高度是设计假设，未从灰度猜高程。
道路按图中橙线标注；平台入口到北沿观景点的小段通路为后补设计。剖面为规划高度，不声称已完成真实行走。
原生POI快照原先正确记录elevation=80，却把markerBaseY错误设为地形0；现显式海拔同时驱动标记几何与视线采样。该修复不消除真实遮挡。
修正目标高度后，台地中央1.5m标记仍被80m台地自身前缘挡住；看见高台的Pull关系改为真实南向台地柱体立面，而非将中央标记当作整座高台。
从台地中央向下看湖同样被自身台面挡住。观察点移到北沿实际支柱顶面内侧0.25m，以新增平台短路接入入口，保留原Pull≥0.25、出生湖面≤0.15、抵达湖面≥0.5的关系要求。
limitations: 原图未严格保持纯色及不透明地面；已保存alpha/色彩统计。
俯视图不能证明先藏后露，使用实际几何射线补充检验。
高台Pull以一段真实前缘立面代表目标线索，不意味着整个台地或中央标记均可见。
观景位置依赖当前12m台地离散：记录其源轮廓及实际支柱；改变cellSize需要重新检查位置支撑和遮挡，不能沿用比例。

pull.meaning: 真实80m台地前缘立面；不是空气中的代理靶

negative.meaning: 加高原提取山肩轮廓，实际遮挡目标及后湖

title: 弯峡谷与支谷：初见、暂隐、再见
prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. One square ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP-DOWN level-planning map, no perspective, text, labels, shadows, textures, trees or buildings. Flat colors: rock/mountain footprint #777F89, water #39A9DB, open ground #EFEAD8, walking paths #E4A33B, usable destination terrace #BB65CE, start dot #E65050. Use few clear irregular polygons and smooth continuous paths, with generous margins. All geometry must be legible for contour extraction. Not radial rings. C02 BENT CANYON AND BRANCH VALLEY: A winding north-south canyon with a narrow river continues from bottom to top. Rock walls form an asymmetrical S-shaped negative space. On the eastern side a branch valley opens around a rock spur to a purple destination terrace. Orange main-bank route starts at bottom and continues through the main canyon; a connected branch path leaves it, enters the side valley, and reaches the purple terrace. Arrange the rock spur so the branch terrace can be glimpsed approaching, hidden behind the spur on the bend, then revealed at the side-valley entrance (Pull and conceal/reveal). Keep main continuation distinct. Vary corridor width into constriction and opening; keep foreground middle rock spur and distant walls for depth. The terrace and route should be at valley floor for unambiguous plan connectivity.

annotations.note: 橙/蓝色区域给出走向；中心线、流向、连接节点由人工语义标注。蓝色图像提取在狭窄处断成两块，显式连接该段，不伪装为自动恢复。
顶视图未提供高度；峡壁/山肩/台地高度是待验证的参数假设，颜色深浅未用作海拔。
初见位置显式抬高6米，并让接近/暂隐路线沿同一缓坡升降；地势不再从轮廓归属组隐式推导。
视觉目标是台地面向来路的真实前缘柱面，场所入口仍独立组织；不是要求从谷底看穿台地看见顶面的小标记。比例由compileStudy和StudyAudit对真实盒体重算，失败必须保留。

limitations: 仅规划几何；不声明真实行走、坡度、通路全程净空或用户审美通过。
仅提取面积超过1000 m²的主山体；小灰色碎片大多沿河路边缘，未赋予地貌语义，未自动生为散柱。
多边形简化的最大顶点偏差逐项记录；柱格边缘误差由cellSize控制。

title: 多支流湖湾
prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. One square ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP-DOWN level-planning map, no perspective, text, labels, shadows, textures, trees or buildings. Flat colors: rock/mountain footprint #777F89, water #39A9DB, open ground #EFEAD8, walking paths #E4A33B, usable destination terrace #BB65CE, start dot #E65050. Use few clear irregular polygons and smooth continuous paths, with generous margins. All geometry must be legible for contour extraction. Not radial rings. C03 MULTIPLE TRIBUTARIES AND LAKE PLACE: Two distinct northern mountain valleys carry two connected blue tributary rivers. They merge at one shared junction and one downstream reach enters a broad irregular central lake. Draw the water as one continuous connected network. A purple usable lakeside terrace occupies dry land on the east bank and joins a clearly orange shore path starting south of the lake. Two-bank connection crosses the narrow common river reach upstream of the lake mouth via exactly one orange bridge. Main walking route connects the lakeside terrace and the bridge, never ends in water. The lake is intentional visual empty space, mountains frame it at different distances. The two incoming valleys are readable from the terrace. No bridges across the widest lake.

annotations: Mountain and lake footprints follow extracted polygons; all vertical dimensions, profiles and observation heights are authored.
water-002 is semantically split into two tributaries and a common stem. Orange bridge pixels hide, rather than terminate, that stem.
water-001 is clipped at image y=520 for the lake; its narrower northern neck belongs to the main river. The river terminates inside the lake at image (662,554).
River centerlines and road centerlines are manually traced from the viewed image; region masks provide area contours only.
The image ends its orange route at the western bridgehead. A 31.6 m bank connector is explicitly authored to a dry western anchor.
mountain-007 is excluded: its 86.5 square metre sliver lies on the road edge and does not read as a separate mountain in the viewed image.
Shared river nodes are authoritative. fitTerrain=false preserves the annotated levels, so a deliberately wrong lake inlet remains detectable.

The low lakeshore eye sees the lake but not the upstream tributaries in the baseline ray sample. Partial views of both tributaries are instead inspected from the bridgehead; this limitation is retained rather than reported as a shore-view success.
The lake level control also changes the river inlet level. Confluence X moves one node shared by all three reaches without changing references.
limitations: Image colors do not establish height, hydraulic flow, physical traversability, or visual quality.
The source image uses an exaggerated-width bridge icon. Its authored crossing extends to explicit dry-bank nodes.
Mountains are a finite-resolution column approximation. Boundary occupancy can expand by at most one cell diagonal.
The lake bottom and river bed are terrain cuts. This case does not implement hydraulic simulation or validate real character movement.
Observer views collectively inspect lake, tributaries and bridge. They do not claim the whole winding network is visible from every eye position.

title: 低谷与高脊：分叉、不同抵达、同处汇合
prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. One square ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP-DOWN level-planning map, no perspective, text, labels, shadows, textures, trees or buildings. Flat colors: rock/mountain footprint #777F89, water #39A9DB, open ground #EFEAD8, walking paths #E4A33B, usable destination terrace #BB65CE, start dot #E65050. Use few clear irregular polygons and smooth continuous paths, with generous margins. All geometry must be legible for contour extraction. Not radial rings. C04 VALLEY/RIDGE TWO ROUTES REJOIN: An elongated irregular mountain separates a western low valley route from an eastern high ridge route. At a clear southern fork, orange walking paths split. The western route follows a narrow river valley and is relatively short/enclosed. The eastern path takes a longer smooth ascent on the rock shoulder, visits a purple viewing terrace on the ridge, then returns to the same northern mountain pass as the western route. BOTH orange lines must visibly share the same fork and rejoin nodes; exactly one loop, not two unrelated disconnected roads. Start dot just south of fork. The ridge terrace overlooks a separate eastern basin as arrival feedback. Rock shapes give different views to the two branches and a distinctive notch at rejoin. No concentric rings or ornamental tiny roads.

provenance.extraction: HSV masks and contour tracing; topology/height/observer semantics assisted by AI

semanticClip.reason: low-saturation shadow tail joins the true north wall to orange low-valley ground; explicit semantic crop, not automatic recovery

annotations: The PNG supplies horizontal colour contours. Heights, profiles, water levels, shared nodes, route centrelines, and observer aims are explicit authored design additions.

Both visible orange branches are split at usable places, but share the exact south-fork and north-rejoin routeNode positions and elevations. Node heights take precedence over cached route profile endpoints.

Every extracted hole retained in a selected semantic mass is explicit as StudyMass.holes; central mountain-001 preserves both transparent holes, including its large interior void. The north wall gray component is explicitly cropped at image y=242 to remove a connected ground-shadow tail and its out-of-scope pinhole; original extracted data remains unchanged.
Orange route placement follows the image. The eastern route gains a continuous authored height profile and a 30m broad supporting shoulder through existing native ridgeBody/solidSupport geometry.
Only the western main river is traced. The separated northern blue patch is joined behind the northern pass through explicitly annotated controls; the image alone does not recover water topology.
The eastern lake footprint comes from water-001. Its visible rock-island colour hole is occupied by the separately extracted mountain-007 rather than interpreted as a dry hole in the lake polygon.

The western low stop is an added place along the orange route, distinct from a graph junction; the eastern place follows the actual purple outline. Its standing point is authored near the east edge at image (970,541), so the platform surface does not block the downward lake view.
Ridge-height updates the platform, route contact profiles, shared high-place node, place elevation and authored observer height together. Fork-X edits one authoritative shared node.
limitations: This case demonstrates image-grounded editable planning geometry and measured views; it does not establish character traversal, collision clearance, good aesthetics, or hydraulic simulation.
Column-cell approximation preserves explicit holes by omitting every intersecting cell. Its maximum hole expansion is sqrt(2) times cellSize; no solid columns are inserted to close the gap.
The northern shared pass crosses the continued river region. Both branches share its actual XYZ, but a production crossing asset and full dry landing proof are not supplied.
The image does not prove the ridge branch is longer or higher. Height is authored and route lengths are measured after compilation; do not claim source-image elevation recovery.
Only eight meaningful extracted regions are assigned mass semantics. Small peripheral gray fragments are retained in extracted/regions.json but not silently turned into extra mountains.
View relations use nine actual target samples. Their fractions describe these samples, not perceptual salience or a complete visibility field.

title: C05 锁区续接与回望
prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. This is C05 semantic world-extension planning. Starting from this top-down level planning map, extend the canvas to the NORTH (upward) by about half the existing height. Preserve the entire existing lower map: its river shape, existing purple high terrace, orange crossing and climbing route, mountain silhouettes and starting dot. In the NEW upper area add an irregular connected valley, a winding river outlet joining the previously existing upper-left lake, a rock ridge continuing a mountain boundary, and a new purple lakeside place. Add an orange path from the old high terrace, passing the old lake and through a clear pass into the new valley and place. Show a second connector back into the old valley to support mental-map recognition and return. Keep the same simple flat gray mountains, blue water, orange paths, purple destinations. All background must be fully opaque light beige #EFEAD8. No labels, no decorative buildings, no perspective, no text. The purpose is testing semantic interface continuation and arrival feedback with the existing area locked, not repainting the old map.
